what_would_change_verdict: Up: dated service records including brake fluid and coolant, plus a Mazda dealer printout showing transmission warranty work or a later revised gearbox, and closed recalls.
Up: a meaningful price reduction toward the fair-value band.

Down: grinding or popping out of gear, damp carpets or drain corrosion, rodent-chewed wiring, or tires older than six years.
evidence.mission_note: It meets the hard requirements (manual, in budget, Mazda reliability), but it is the ruled-out Sport trim in ruled-out red on the riskiest gearbox build. It would only serve as a pragmatic bridge, not as the RF he is targeting.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: a full VIN whose decode matches a 2016 MX-5 Sport soft top with the 2.0L, a manual transmission, and a history summary claiming one owner and no reported accidents. It provides no maintenance evidence at all: no records, no brake-fluid or coolant dates, no transmission history, and no recall-closure proof. That matters on a 10-year-old car from the early-2016 6MT production period. The photos show a clean, apparently stock exterior and engine bay. They also show a torn section of the underhood insulation pad and surface corrosion on the brake rotors, which suggest a period of sitting or possible rodent activity. The spec conflicts directly with the buyer's preferences: Sport trim and red paint are both ruled out, and it is a soft top rather than an RF. The $20,995 out-the-door price is roughly 15% above the $18,271 fair-value mid for comparable soft-top ND1s. Gearbox health, cabin water ingress, tire age and recall status remain open.
